holidays.name: National Pizza Day
holidays.description: A cheesy celebration of one of the world's most beloved foods, when pizzerias across the United States offer deals, specials, and free slices to anyone willing to say yes to pepperoni.
holidays.origin: National Pizza Day is an unofficial American food holiday with unclear origins. It gained popularity in the 2000s through restaurant promotions and social media, and the date has been widely observed on February 9.
holidays.funFact: Americans eat roughly 3 billion pizzas a year, which works out to about 350 slices per second.

holidays.name: National Bagels and Lox Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the classic combo of a chewy bagel, silky smoked salmon, cream cheese, capers, and red onion, a breakfast that makes any morning feel fancy.
holidays.origin: Bagels and lox grew out of Jewish immigrant communities in New York City in the early 20th century, where the pairing became a brunch staple. The day is an informal food observance, celebrated mainly in the US.
holidays.funFact: Traditional bagels are boiled before being baked, which gives them their signature chewy crust and dense interior.

holidays.name: Read in the Bathtub Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to filling the tub, grabbing a good book, and soaking while you read, with extra points for avoiding dropping your novel into the water.
holidays.origin: This is a lighthearted unofficial observance that appears on many quirky-holiday calendars. It seems to have been created to encourage relaxation and reading, with no single known founder.
holidays.funFact: The ancient Romans were big fans of reading and socializing at public baths, so bathing with a book has historical street cred.

holidays.name: Toothache Day
holidays.description: A day that, rather unfortunately, commemorates the pain of toothaches. It is a reminder to check in with your dentist before your molars file a complaint.
holidays.origin: Toothache Day is an unofficial observance listed in quirky holiday calendars, tied to encouraging good dental care and not putting off those checkups. Its exact origin is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Tooth decay is one of the most common chronic diseases in the world, affecting billions of people.

holidays.name: Safer Internet Day (around this time of year)
holidays.description: A global day when people, schools, and organizations promote using technology responsibly, kindly, and safely, ideally without falling for a prince who needs gift cards.
holidays.origin: Safer Internet Day began in 2004 as an initiative of the EU SafeBorders project and was soon taken up by the Insafe network. It is celebrated in early February, and in 2021 it fell on February 9, with the date varying year to year as the second day of the second week of February.
holidays.funFact: The event is now celebrated in well over 100 countries, which makes it one of the most widely observed online-safety days on Earth.
